idiom_name: hand-written dispatcher: step registry (dict of callables) + session-carried step
implementation_notes: Neither the standard library nor the dominant frameworks own flow decisions - Django's URLconf is a front controller and its views are page controllers - so the Application Controller is hand-written: a module-level STEPS registry mapping step ids to callables that read the request, perform the step's command and return the next step id, with the current step and the partial data kept in the session and a single view that dispatches and renders the step's template. What replaces the classic structure is that dict plus one dispatch function: the command objects become the callables, the view reference is derived from the step id. Reach for this when the flow is not screen-sequential or when third-party dependencies are unwelcome; for the classic multi-step form case the django-formtools wizard supplies the same centralisation as a library (see the second variant), and python-statemachine or transitions add explicit guards and callbacks if you want the machine spelled out.
pitfalls: Session state is shared by tabs: two in-flight requests can interleave transitions, so validate that the submitted step matches the stored one and make each step idempotent (POST/redirect/GET plus a per-step token).
Lambdas in a module-level dict are opaque to debuggers and cannot be serialized or introspected; a class per step with a name and docstring pays for itself as soon as the flow grows.
Deriving the template path from the step id makes a typo a TemplateDoesNotExist late in the flow - keep step ids in an enum and assert the registry covers it at import time.

variants.name: django-formtools SessionWizardView (declarative FORMS dict)
variants.implementation_notes: django-formtools turns the wizard case into a library: SessionWizardView subclass defines form_list (an ordered list of step name and form class) that declares the flow, condition_dict adds branches, dispatch() reads the current step from the storage backend, render_next_step()/render_goto_step() move through it and done() runs the final command. This replaces the hand-written dispatcher completely for multi-step forms - the step sequence is data, the storage (session or cookie) is pluggable, and each step already has a template convention - so prefer it whenever the flow is a sequence of validated forms; a hand-written controller is still needed for flows that are not form-shaped.
pitfalls: The wizard advances when the step's form validates, so a step whose legality depends on more than its own form needs a condition_dict entry (or a guard in done()) - otherwise users are led through steps that do not apply.
Storage is the conversation state: the session backend is per-browser but not concurrency-safe, and the cookie backend serializes the data client-side - never put secrets in wizard step data.
